```{r}
#| label: packages
library(BHAI)
library(plotly)
library(gt)

hai <- c("HAP", "SSI", "BSI", "UTI", "CDI") # order used in the paper
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| cache: true
data(german_pps_2011_repr)
germany <- PPS(num_hai_patients=num_hai_patients, num_hai_patients_by_stratum=num_hai_patients_by_stratum,
    num_hai_patients_by_stratum_prior=num_hai_patients_by_stratum_prior, num_survey_patients=num_survey_patients,
    length_of_stay=length_of_stay, loi_pps=loi_pps, mccabe_scores_distr=mccabe_scores_distr,
    mccabe_life_exp=mccabe_life_exp, hospital_discharges=hospital_discharges, population=population,
    country="German PPS")

data(eu_pps_2011) # loads eu_pps

set.seed(2026)
res_de <- bhai(germany, nsim=1000)
res_eu <- bhai(eu_pps, nsim=1000)
```

```{r}
#| label: totals
tot_de <- res_de@bhai_summary$ALL$TOTAL[, "50%"] # medians for all five HAIs
tot_eu <- res_eu@bhai_summary$ALL$TOTAL[, "50%"]
per100k_de <- tot_de / sum(res_de@population) * 1e5
per100k_eu <- tot_eu / sum(res_eu@population) * 1e5
gap <- round((per100k_de / per100k_eu - 1) * 100) # % difference, Germany vs EU/EEA
```

Scrubbing up before surgery is one of medicine's oldest rituals, and one of its most effective. Before every operation, surgeons spend minutes washing their hands and forearms, because a single contaminated hand can carry bacteria straight into a patient's body during the procedure.

![Two medical professionals scrubbing their hands before surgery.](thumbnail.jpg){fig-alt=""}

Even so, hospitals remain a place where people catch infections. On any given day, about one in 18 patients in a European hospital has at least one infection acquired during their stay (ECDC, 2013). These are called healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), infections that develop in hospital and are unrelated to the reason for admission. A procedure can go perfectly, and the patient can still develop a urinary tract infection from a catheter a few days later. In Germany, an estimated 20 to 30% of HAIs are preventable (Gastmeier et al., 2010), but prevention resources are limited, so knowing which infections cause the most harm matters as much as knowing how many there are.

Germany is a particularly interesting case: per hospitalised patient, its infection rate is below the European average; across the whole population however, Germans lose more years of healthy life to HAIs than the European average. This post looks at three questions: how large the burden of HAIs in Germany is, which infections drive it, and how a lower risk per patient can still produce a higher burden overall.

## How big is the problem?



```{r}
#| label: tbl-germany
#| tbl-cap: "Annual burden of five types of HAI, German PPS sample, Germany, 2011. Median and 95% uncertainty interval."
tab1 <- bhai.prettyTable(res_de)[c(hai, "ALL"), ]
tab1 <- data.frame(HAI=c(hai, "All"), tab1)

gt(tab1) |>
    cols_label(Cases="HAIs", Deaths="Attributable deaths", DALY="DALYs", YLL="YLLs", YLD="YLDs") |>
    tab_style(style=cell_text(weight="bold"), locations=cells_body(rows=HAI == "All")) |>
    tab_options(table.background.color="#ffffff", column_labels.font.weight="bold", container.padding.y=px(0))
```

## The most common infection is not the most deadly



```{r}
#| label: fig-cases-deaths
#| fig-cap: "Annual number of HAIs (left) and attributable deaths (right) by type of infection, Germany, 2011."
fig1 <- data.frame(hai=factor(hai, levels=hai), cases=NA, deaths=NA)
for (i in 1:5) {
    fig1$cases[i] <- res_de@bhai_summary[[hai[i]]]$TOTAL["Cases", "50%"]
    fig1$deaths[i] <- res_de@bhai_summary[[hai[i]]]$TOTAL["Deaths", "50%"]
}

cases_plot <- plot_ly(fig1, x=~hai, y=~cases / 1000, type="bar", marker=list(color="#00759C"),
    text=~format(round(cases), big.mark=","), textposition="none",
    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{text} infections<extra></extra>")
deaths_plot <- plot_ly(fig1, x=~hai, y=~deaths, type="bar", marker=list(color="#00759C"),
    text=~format(round(deaths), big.mark=","), textposition="none",
    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{text} deaths<extra></extra>")

subplot(cases_plot, deaths_plot, titleY=TRUE, margin=0.08) |>
    layout(showlegend=FALSE, yaxis=list(title="Infections (thousands)"), yaxis2=list(title="Attributable deaths")) |>
    config(displayModeBar=FALSE)
```

## Germany compared with the rest of Europe



```{r}
#| label: fig-europe
#| fig-cap: "Annual burden of five types of HAI: (left) attributable deaths per 100,000 population and (right) DALYs per 100,000 population, Germany and EU/EEA, 2011–2012. Error bars show the 95% uncertainty interval."
fig2 <- data.frame()
for (s in c("German PPS", "ECDC PPS (EU/EEA)")) {
    res <- if (s=="German PPS") res_de else res_eu
    k <- 1e5 / sum(res@population)
    for (i in hai) {
        tot <- res@bhai_summary[[i]]$TOTAL[c("Deaths", "DALY"), ] * k
        fig2 <- rbind(fig2, data.frame(sample=s, hai=i, measure=c("Deaths", "DALY"),
            low=tot[, "2.5%"], mid=tot[, "50%"], high=tot[, "97.5%"]))
    }
}
fig2$hai <- factor(fig2$hai, levels=hai)

burden_plot <- function(m, y_title, legend) {
    de <- subset(fig2, sample == "German PPS" & measure == m)
    eu <- subset(fig2, sample == "ECDC PPS (EU/EEA)" & measure == m)
    label <- function(d) paste0(round(d$mid, 1), " (", round(d$low, 1), "–", round(d$high, 1), ")")
    hover <- paste0("<b>%{x}</b><br>", y_title, ": %{text}<extra></extra>")
    plot_ly() |>
        add_bars(data=de, x=~hai, y=~mid, name="German PPS", marker=list(color="#B43E1D"),
            legendgroup="de", showlegend=legend, text=label(de), textposition="none", hovertemplate=hover,
            error_y=list(array=de$high - de$mid, arrayminus=de$mid - de$low, color="black")) |>
        add_bars(data=eu, x=~hai, y=~mid, name="ECDC PPS (EU/EEA)", marker=list(color="#E3AF45"),
            legendgroup="eu", showlegend=legend, text=label(eu), textposition="none", hovertemplate=hover,
            error_y=list(array=eu$high - eu$mid, arrayminus=eu$mid - eu$low, color="black")) |>
        layout(yaxis=list(title=y_title))
}

subplot(burden_plot("Deaths", "Attributable deaths per 100,000", TRUE),
    burden_plot("DALY", "DALYs per 100,000", FALSE), titleY=TRUE, margin=0.08) |>
    layout(barmode="group", legend=list(orientation="h", x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=1.12)) |>
    config(displayModeBar=FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-europe
#| tbl-cap: "Annual burden per 100,000 population of five types of HAI, German PPS sample and ECDC PPS sample, Germany and EU/EEA, 2011–2012. Median and 95% uncertainty interval."
cols <- c("Cases", "Deaths", "DALY")
tab_de <- t(bhai.prettyTable(res_de, pop_norm=TRUE)[c(hai, "ALL"), cols])
tab_eu <- t(bhai.prettyTable(res_eu, pop_norm=TRUE)[c(hai, "ALL"), cols])

tab2 <- data.frame(
    measure=rep(c("HAIs per 100,000", "Attributable deaths per 100,000", "DALYs per 100,000"), each=2),
    sample=rep(c("German PPS", "ECDC PPS (EU/EEA)"), times=3),
    rbind(tab_de, tab_eu)[c(1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6), ]
)

gt(tab2, groupname_col="measure", rowname_col="sample") |>
    cols_label(ALL="All") |>
    tab_options(table.background.color="#ffffff", column_labels.font.weight="bold", row_group.font.weight="bold",
        container.padding.y=px(0))
```
